title: Risk-Bounded Distribution Reconstruction: Stable Statistic Calibration for Long-Tailed Recognition
claim: A frozen-feature pipeline calibrates class statistics with risk-bounded mean and covariance updates, turning unreliable tail estimates into separable distributions.
layout: Snake-shaped flow in two rows, shaded stage regions, mini scatter and geometry insets
description: A two-row, snake-shaped flow diagram with shaded background regions. The top-left shows a long-tailed bar chart of head and tail classes with dot clusters. An arrow leads to a backbone icon, then to a frozen-features snowflake box. Next comes a feature-space scatter plot with colored ellipses and stars for class means, and a tail class highlighted in red. It then leads to a Risk-Bounded Mean Calibration panel in which star points flow through a barrier labeled Supportive Projection to a red risk-bounded update star. The flow turns downward into Covariance Calibration. That stage has boxes for head-guided shrinkage, calibrated tail distribution and an optional diffusion variant, plus a 3D rival-subspace contraction sketch. It continues left to a reconstructed distribution plot and ends in a Stage-2 classifier panel with Voronoi-like decision regions. Pastel blue and orange backgrounds separate the stages. Stars and ellipses use consistent colors across panels.
caption: Overview of RBDR. After Stage-1 training, the backbone is frozen and class-wise statistics are estimated in the feature space.
abstract: Long-tailed recognition suffers from extreme class imbalance, where scarce tail data leads to biased and fragile feature distributions that exacerbate confusion with semantically or visually similar classes. Prior feature-space reconstruction methods transfer head-class structure or train conditional generators to synthesize tail features, yet the resulting \emph{statistical} updates are often heuristic and can degrade multi-class separability when tail estimates are unreliable. Given this issue, we propose \emph{Risk-Bounded Distribution Reconstruction} (RBDR), an offline statistic calibration framework for the two-stage long-tailed pipeline, grounded in an analysis of rival-induced discriminative directions. RBDR performs (i) risk-aware mean calibration by softly projecting any candidate update onto a supportive set such that a surrogate discriminative-risk upper bound does not increase, and (ii) covariance control by shrinking dispersion in a rival subspace while preserving diversity in orthogonal components. In the frozen-feature reconstruction setting, these calibration components convert heuristic reconstruction cues into controllable distributional updates, improving both performance and stability across multiple long-tailed benchmarks.
